full_name: Problem Gambling Severity Index (9 items of the CPGI)
developer_doi: NA (Ferris & Wynne 2001, CPGI final report, no DOI)
threshold_source: Categories 0 non-problem, 1-2 low risk, 3-7 moderate risk, 8+ problem gambling (Ferris & Wynne 2001); validity of the categories and revised thresholds 1-4 / 5-7 / 8+ (Currie et al. 2013, 10.1007/s10899-012-9300-6)
notes: Revised thresholds used in sensitivity analysis 4. CPGI = PGSI for scoring. CPGI, its French version ICJE (Indice canadien du jeu excessif) and versions with items reworded for sports betting score as the PGSI if the item scoring (0-3, total 0-27) is unchanged; other scoring (e.g., the Turkish PSBSI, items 1-3, total 9-27) = adhoc

threshold_source: Lesieur & Blume 1987: 5+ probable pathological gambler; 3-4 commonly labelled problem or at-risk
notes: Lifetime or past-year versions: time frame coded

full_name: South Oaks Gambling Screen - Revised for Adolescents
threshold_source: Winters, Stinchfield & Fulkerson 1993: 0-1 no problem, 2-3 at risk, 4+ problem gambling

full_name: NORC DSM-IV Screen for Gambling Problems
developer_doi: NA (Gerstein et al. 1999, report, no DOI)
threshold_source: 1-2 at risk, 3-4 problem, 5+ pathological (Gerstein et al. 1999); psychometrics: Hodgins 2004, 10.1016/j.addbeh.2004.03.017

full_name: NODS Control, Lying and Preoccupation items
threshold_source: Toce-Gerstein, Gerstein & Volberg 2009: rapid screen, any positive item

full_name: DSM-IV criteria for pathological gambling, self-report (e.g., Stinchfield measure)
threshold_source: DSM-IV: 5+ pathological gambling; 3-4 commonly labelled problem gambling; Stinchfield 2003 validation

full_name: DSM-5 criteria for gambling disorder, self-report
threshold_source: DSM-5: 4-5 mild, 6-7 moderate, 8-9 severe gambling disorder; threshold lowered from 5 to 4 (Petry et al. 2013, 10.1111/j.1360-0443.2012.04087.x)
notes: L2 for DSM-5 screens stays provisional: no included report gave a DSM-5 category below 4 at full-text screening; an estimate below 4 is coded L2 with the note "DSM-5 L2 provisional"

threshold_source: Williams & Volberg 2014: recreational / at-risk / problem / pathological
Gebauer, LaBrie & Shaffer 2010: any positive item = possible gambling disorder
Johnson et al. 1997: one or two positive answers

full_name: Canadian Adolescent Gambling Inventory, General Problem Severity Subscale (GPSS, 9 items)
developer_doi: NA (Tremblay, Stinchfield, Wiebe & Wynne 2010, CAGI Phase III final report, no DOI)
threshold_source: GPSS 0-1 no problem (green light), 2-5 low to moderate severity (yellow light), 6+ high severity (red light); cut-off 6 Se 0.93, Sp 0.99 (Jimenez-Murcia et al. 2017, 10.3389/fpsyg.2017.00177, citing Tremblay et al. 2010)
notes: Adolescent samples. Yellow light is the instrument's at-risk category (L2); green light includes a score of 1, so L1 is not defined
